note: Sources used by GEMSDOE46. 'supports' states exactly what was taken from each source. Sources that could not be reached from this sandbox are marked so; nothing in this repository is presented as verified if it could not be checked.

sources.title: DrivenData competition 306 - GEMS Prize Challenge, problem description (metric, submission format, task definition)
supports: DTI(alpha=0.2, beta=0.8) with triangular kernel k(d)=max(1-d/R,0), R=300 m
the three distance-weighted terms TPw / FPw / FNw as transcribed in src/gems46/metric.py
the worked example TPw=3.00, FPw=1.89, FNw=2.00 -> 0.60 (arithmetic reproduced in tests/test_metric.py)
submission format: single-band float32 GeoTIFF, EPSG:32611, 100 m, same bounds, values in [0,1], null/NaN outside
two-round structure: initial round scored on a private set of expert-labelled *new* faults; final round rescored on an expanded label set after expert review of submitted predictions

sources.title: DrivenData forum thread 11516 - 'Scoring clarification: are known USGS/INGENIOUS faults masked when scoring, and are they in the Final Round label set?'
supports: DrivenData staff (chrisk-dd, 2026-09-16): 'Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms'
same reply: 'Re-evaluation will also mask/exclude the existing USGS/INGENIOUS faults'

consequence implemented in src/gems46/metric.py: predictions on/near masked pixels earn no credit but predicting *on* them is neutral; predicting within the 300 m kernel of them still pays the partial FP tax

sources.title: Peng, C.-K., Buldyrev, S. V., Havlin, S., Simons, M., Stanley, H. E., Goldberger, A. L. (1994). Mosaic organization of DNA nucleotides. Physical Review E 49(5), 1685-1689
supports: origin of detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA): integrate the series, split into boxes of length n, remove the local least-squares line in each box, take the RMS fluctuation F(n), and take the slope of log F(n) vs log n as the scaling exponent alpha
the estimator implemented in src/gems46/dfa.py follows this definition exactly (verified against an independent O(N) transcription in tests/test_dfa.py)

sources.title: Varotsos, P. A., Sarlis, N. V., Skordas, E. S. (2009). Detrended fluctuation analysis of the magnetic and electric field variations that precede rupture. Chaos 19(2), 023114
supports: pre-rupture magnetic field variations appear random at short time lags and become long-range correlated at lags above the mean inter-spike interval, with scaling exponent alpha around 0.9
pre-seismic electric field variations of several hours to days show scale invariance with alpha approximately 1 over about five orders of magnitude

IMPORTANT NUANCE (recorded so the hypothesis is not overstated): the paper's shift is a *crossover in time lag* within a time series - not a demonstration that a spatial scaling exponent changes across a geological fault. GEMSDOE46 adapts DFA to transects of a spatial grid; that adaptation is this project's hypothesis (H46-1), not a published result.
